newsitem.title: USA: Perrigo says '98 sales growth to match '97.
newsitem.headline: Perrigo says '98 sales growth to match '97.

text.p: Perrigo Co said Wednesday it expected margins to be about flat in fiscal year 1998 and sales growth for 1998 to be the same as 1997.

"Looking forward, in fiscal 1998 we expect sales growth to approximate the growth experienced in 1997," chairman and chief executive Mike Jandernoa said in a statement. "And, with pricing in all product categories remaining highly competitive through next year, we expect margins to remain in the same range as fiscal 1997."

Earlier Perrigo said it earned $9 million, or $0.12 a share, in the fourth quarter ended June 30 versus $4.9 million, or $0.06 a share, in the same period last year. Net sales rose 12 percent to $196.2 million.
Last year's fourth quarter results included $2.6 million in restructuring costs compared to $926,000 in restructuring costs during the same period this year.

"Sales for fiscal 1997 were a new record and included increases in cough and cold, analgesic, antacid and vitamin products as well as new products such as Minoxidil and Naproxen Sodium. Our higher sales of OTC products, strong vitamin sales and improved margins in personal care, along with continuing employee task force cost reduction progress, helped to increase gross profits at a faster rate than sales," Jandernoa said.

"We also anticipate higher capital spending in 1998. In addition to the Greenville project, we will invest in a new business software system and new distribution centers in Michigan and Tennessee to replace current leased space," he said. The new facilities were expected to be operational by the start of the next fiscal year, he added.
